audit_scope: Papers V–VIII traditional editions; executable finite machinery and explicit runtime boundaries, not a proof audit

sources.title: Paper VI: Transfer Semigroups and Memory
Paper VII: Quantum Seeds and Effective Dynamics

mechanisms.summary: Residue coordinates, refinement addresses, and FIR transfer reindexing
boundaries: Finite arrays/FIR kernels; boundary modes must be specified. Bilateral infinite sequence and Hilbert-space convergence claims remain mathematical theorems.

mechanisms.summary: General integer-matrix sublattice cosets and polyphase transfer
boundaries: Runtime lattice phases are rectangular axiswise decimations. Arbitrary B Z^d coset representatives and nested matrix-lattice transfers are absent.

mechanisms.summary: Finite filter-bank reconstruction and predict/update lifting
boundaries: Finite and periodic boundary contracts; NumPy reconstruction residuals use tolerance.

mechanisms.section: E5: frequency-symbol frame and perturbation bounds
mechanisms.summary: Uniform symbol bounds and stable perturbed synthesis
boundaries: Finite matrix checks do not certify essential infimum/supremum over the full frequency circle. No general Laurent-symbol uniform frame-bound verifier.

mechanisms.summary: Haar packet reconstruction and additive admissible best bases
boundaries: Finite dyadic Haar trees and additive supplied leaf costs; no unrestricted basis discovery.

mechanisms.summary: Optimal pruning gap and local error envelope
boundaries: No dedicated arbitrary-objective perturbation/error-envelope API. Compiler decision gaps concern solved child scores and finite additive models.

mechanisms.summary: Retained singular packets and cancellation of supplied jumps
boundaries: Supplied traces/jumps and approximation operator. Encoding them does not verify Sobolev membership or discover all singularities of an arbitrary function.

mechanisms.summary: Mask, amplitude, overlap-matrix, and location error formulas
boundaries: Uses supplied measures and amplitudes. Geometry/tube hypotheses remain unchecked; TruncatedPowerTerm location bound is coarser than the sharp integrated E8.3 formula.

mechanisms.summary: Conditional recovery of separated jumps, Haar localization, and annihilating differences
boundaries: Lipschitz, jump separation, amplitude, and noise hypotheses are model inputs. Subgaussian probability uses the declared noise model; sample output alone does not prove it.

mechanisms.summary: Finite retained-edge versus Fourier approximation and data-driven packet estimates
boundaries: Finite examples and threshold estimator are not universal two-dimensional edge recovery or statistical consistency.

mechanisms.summary: Residue convolution of nonlinear products and shifted filters
boundaries: Finite coefficient/channel model; formal and infinite Cauchy products require the paper hypotheses.

mechanisms.summary: Cayley/Smith cyclic phase coordinates and sensitivity
boundaries: Finite affine charts only; projective infinity, homogeneous-pair equality, and boundary singularities are not represented by these numerical chart functions.

mechanisms.summary: Universal stable edge recovery and adaptive statistical consistency
boundaries: The paper identifies conjectural extensions. A finite test framework cannot implement a proof of them.

mechanisms.summary: Matrix evolution, packet block convolution, resolvents, and minimum transfer order
boundaries: Finite numerical matrix exponentials/resolvents. No general Dyson path-simplex executor; MatrixSemigroup.at accepts nonnegative time only.

mechanisms.summary: Generator, semigroup, and resolvent refinement defects
boundaries: Duhamel evaluation uses numerical Gauss-Legendre quadrature. Finite generator residuals do not establish infinite defect summability or a projective-limit semigroup.

mechanisms.summary: Weighted reconstruction, range closure, projective limits, and generator domains
boundaries: Runtime records a finite prefix only. Infinite tail control, closed reconstruction range, and compatible generator-domain conditions remain external mathematics. Summed finite defects alone do not prove a limit.

mechanisms.summary: Stochastic operators, exact lumpability, finite-horizon errors and reversible coarse dynamics
boundaries: Finite numerical matrices with explicit row/column convention. Reversibility descent/Dirichlet-form identities can be checked from matrices but have no dedicated general theorem API.

mechanisms.summary: Weighted conditional expectation, tower laws, and martingale energy packets
boundaries: Finite partitions and weights; does not construct infinite filtrations or establish their convergence.

mechanisms.summary: Exact rational Gaussian moments, OU generator and polynomial transfer
boundaries: New exact real-rational finite polynomial machinery. Correlation rho is rational in [0,1]; rho=e^-t is a convention, not an exact evaluation for arbitrary t. Degree/order caps raise without truncation. Infinite Lp positivity, Hermite completeness and strong reconstruction remain theorems.

mechanisms.summary: Fractional OU number-operator transfer on infinite Hermite packets
boundaries: A finite diagonal multiplier can be supplied to the matrix API; there is no infinite Hermite-series convergence or fractional Gaussian-function evaluator.

mechanisms.summary: Bayesian packet reconstruction, sufficiency, distortion, and information decomposition
boundaries: Exact profile equality and approximate clustering are separate. Part I mass-only criterion requires at least two blocks; E9.2 additionally preserves within-block conditional distributions, so its one-block case is stronger. Finite floating likelihoods and positive-evidence contracts.

mechanisms.summary: Replicator/evidence flow and hidden-Markov filtering
boundaries: Finite state space. Uniform likelihood bounds and exact lumpability are hypotheses; numerical finite recursion is not universal filtering consistency.

mechanisms.summary: Self-adjoint fractional powers, naturality and common-positive-gap defect bounds
boundaries: Hermitian positive finite matrices and numerical eigendecomposition. fractional_defect requires a common strictly positive gap for the Lipschitz bound; it does not implement the main-text gapless Holder estimate.

mechanisms.summary: Gapless Holder estimate and stable/Poisson subordination measures
boundaries: No executable general gapless Holder-bound helper or stable subordination-measure/quadrature implementation. Sectorial/nonnormal domain control is external.

mechanisms.summary: One-dimensional Dirichlet Green reconstruction and low-mode control
boundaries: Specific uniform interval grid; smoothness/fourth-derivative bounds supplied. It is not a general-domain elliptic Green solver.

mechanisms.summary: Finite Feynman-Kac path weights, propagation/killing and coarse transfer
boundaries: Column stochastic forward state convention: backward generator Q.T-diag(V), discrete operator diag(exp(-V))@P.T with killing at current states. No arbitrary process/domain path-integral construction.

mechanisms.summary: Schur-Feshbach reduction, self energy, memory, and finite closure moments
boundaries: Finite block systems with invertibility/Laplace-domain guards. Closure uses all hidden-dimensional moments, not only the leading coupling product. Numerical certificates are not exact rational identities.

mechanisms.summary: Finite auxiliary realization of supplied B exp(tD) C kernels
boundaries: Accepts supplied realization matrices, including Jordan blocks. Does not synthesize a realization from an arbitrary strictly proper rational matrix function.

mechanisms.summary: Primary Jordan memory modes and optimal selection for certified modal bound
boundaries: No primary spectral projector/Jordan coefficient extraction or largest-weight modal selector. Largest certified-bound weights need not minimize actual kernel error when modes cancel. Existing matrix exponentials can evaluate supplied Jordan models.

mechanisms.summary: Memory-kernel L1 error and trajectory perturbation bounds
boundaries: Finite rational kernels obtain explicit bounds. Arbitrary callable quadrature needs an independently supplied rigorous integration bound; trajectory norm and mild-solution hypotheses are not inferred.

mechanisms.summary: Phase-type survival, hazard, moments, residual life and competing risks
boundaries: Runtime requires strictly stable transient subgenerator. The paper also permits killed nontransient chains before imposing almost-sure absorption. No monotone-hazard claim.

mechanisms.summary: Canonical finite Taylor-jet functional calculus and bounded holomorphic reciprocal substitution
boundaries: Exponentials, resolvents, and self-adjoint fractional powers are special cases. No general canonical-jet/contour executor with zero-free domain and logarithm-branch validation. Scalar reciprocal APIs in Paper IV are not the operator theorem.

mechanisms.summary: Unbounded/continuum evolution and nonrational infinite memory extensions
boundaries: Finite tests do not establish domains, infinite reconstruction, universal memory approximation, or continuum convergence.

mechanisms.summary: Quantum grammars, local orbit dimensions, Schmidt and observable seed ranks
boundaries: Finite numerical ranks require tolerance and supplied operator grammar. Not an arbitrary infinite algebra module classification.

mechanisms.summary: Finite-group central projectors, cyclic charges and selection rules
boundaries: Supplied representation/characters are mathematical inputs; finite consistency checks use tolerance.

mechanisms.summary: Representation matrix units and nonabelian fusion intertwiners
boundaries: Central projectors do not construct irreducible E_lambda_ij matrix units. Coordinate E_ij utilities are a different object. Clebsch-Gordan/fusion intertwiners are not supplied by a general API.

mechanisms.summary: Coherent packet-path circuit expansion and interference
boundaries: Finite circuit and packet family. Amplitudes must be coherently summed before probabilities; finite paths do not provide infinite circuit convergence.

mechanisms.summary: Moving packets, direct rotations, Kato transport and leakage bounds
boundaries: Numerical one-parameter transport; sampled leakage integration requires quadrature error control. Endpoint projectors do not establish a differentiable path.

mechanisms.summary: Frame connection, curvature two-form, gauge changes and Chern integral
boundaries: One-parameter Kato transport is not a general multiparameter curvature or bundle-topology implementation. No explicit Bloch-sphere Chern-integral API.

mechanisms.summary: Operator packet blocks, Kraus/Choi channels and Lindblad coherence
boundaries: Finite matrices with numerical CP/TP and covariance checks; no infinite channel or unbounded Lindblad generator. Coherence sectors can be inspected but there is no dedicated general coherence-order projector factory.

mechanisms.summary: Knill-Laflamme obstruction, syndrome construction and finite recovery channels
boundaries: Exact-correctability theorem is represented by finite numerical error-span invariant checks. Trace scalar representatives/obstruction norms do not calculate the general infimum-over-scalars approximate-correctability distance or prove arbitrary approximate recovery guarantees.

mechanisms.summary: Correctable observable algebras and commutant criterion
boundaries: QuantumCode implements subspace scalar KL correction, not an arbitrary observable-algebra correctability constructor.

mechanisms.summary: Finite effective Hamiltonians, projected resolvents and oscillatory memory
boundaries: Numerical finite Hermitian blocks and guarded spectral parameters. Runtime memory kernel is -B exp(-itD) B* in psi_dot=-iHpsi form; manuscript positive oscillatory kernel is written in i dpsi/dt form. These conventions must be translated.

mechanisms.summary: Uniform-gap effective/self-energy bounds and positive memory-kernel Gram structure
boundaries: Pointwise evaluations do not certify cutoff-independent gaps or full parameter intervals. No named uniform-gap/stability-bound utilities or positive oscillatory-memory Gram constructor.

mechanisms.summary: Positive transfer, logarithmic generator and finite reflection positivity
boundaries: Finite positive-definite contraction transfer and finite Gram matrices. Does not establish Osterwalder-Schrader regularity, covariance, locality, clustering or field reconstruction.

mechanisms.summary: Finite lattice Laplacians, heat traces, spectral dimension and low-mode bounds
boundaries: Finite lattice curves and low-mode estimates. A spectral-dimension plateau is neither continuum heat-trace convergence nor a physical Einstein/spin-two theorem.

mechanisms.summary: Constraint commutator closure, quotient obstruction and transported defects
boundaries: Checks finite operator-span closure. Common-kernel compression may kill an obstruction without proving operator-span closure; no general unbounded-domain constraint verifier.

mechanisms.summary: Finite Hamiltonian variation reports and bounded direct-limit criteria
boundaries: Runtime uses finitely many Hamiltonians in one common Hilbert space. Increasing-space isometric embeddings, infinite variation tails, trace-norm state limits and limit positivity require external hypotheses.

mechanisms.summary: Continuum constraints, Euclidean fields, Lorentzian theory and Einstein/spin-two criteria
boundaries: These are separately stated milestones/criteria or conjectures, not results implied by finite symmetry, heat traces, reflection-positive Gram matrices, or packet towers.

mechanisms.summary: Finite packet layout and intermediate representation semantics
boundaries: Finite supplied active blocks; inactive block support and output contracts must be explicit. NumPy arithmetic is numerical.

mechanisms.summary: Arithmetic, storage, streaming and roofline model
boundaries: Exact counts/bounds for the declared model, not measured execution or proof of a specific hardware cache/communication schedule.

mechanisms.summary: Dense, diagonal, block, circulant, Toeplitz, Kronecker and Walsh primitives
boundaries: Finite numerical operators and explicit transform normalization; generic higher tensor products can be composed from binary factors.

mechanisms.summary: Thin-factor/BDLR application, product and Woodbury solve
boundaries: Finite factors; inverse requires guarded local/core invertibility. Exact algebraic identity is evaluated numerically.

mechanisms.summary: Small-core QR/SVD recompression and accumulated error bounds
boundaries: Numerical ordered SVD with residuals, not a newly compiled formal proof of SVD existence or a universal rank-discovery algorithm.

mechanisms.summary: Boolean support products, powers, path closure and Schur-fill inclusion
boundaries: Support predicts possible nonzeros; cancellation can remove entries. Inverse helper requires acyclic unit-diagonal support; closure alone does not produce inverse values.

mechanisms.summary: Topological triangular stage schedule and forward block solve
boundaries: Graph stage counts are implemented. No dedicated stagewise block-triangular forward-solve executor from Appendix E.2. Unlimited parallelism/stage model is explicit.

mechanisms.summary: Krylov, CG/Lanczos, block-Jacobi and perturbation estimates
boundaries: Generated curvature checks do not establish global SPD of an arbitrary callable. Conditioning/gap inputs and numerical tolerance remain visible.

mechanisms.summary: Sensitivity bounds, continuous allocation and discrete precision dynamic program
boundaries: Optimal for supplied sensitivity/cost/options and quantized weights. Does not infer overflow, underflow, accumulation precision, or device kernel availability.

mechanisms.summary: Proposed-layout residual and BDLR discovery
boundaries: Threshold support discovery and SVD approximation in a supplied layout. No arbitrary simultaneous commuting-normal joint-eigenspace discovery API or universal profitable-layout search.

mechanisms.summary: Finite additive Lagrangian and quantized-budget tree optimization
boundaries: Finite candidate tree with additive costs/errors/overheads. Budget quantizes each retained leaf independently. No general optimality for overlaps, global rank coupling or nonlocal costs.

mechanisms.summary: Independent bounded exact enumeration of complete admissible prunings
boundaries: New rational oracle enumerates every pruning and never runs the optimized recurrence. Exactness refers to the supplied dyadic float model. Node/depth/pruning caps raise instead of reporting a partial optimum. It independently verifies plan metadata and ignores attached certificates; it cannot prove behavior on unenumerated trees.

mechanisms.summary: Solved keep/split decision gaps
boundaries: Margin reporter uses floating scores; optimized compiler comparisons use exact dyadic arithmetic. Strict gap interpretation near floating ties needs care. Perturbation is of solved scores, not arbitrary raw leaf inputs.

mechanisms.summary: Cached subtree/ancestor-only recompilation
boundaries: Replacing nodes and recompiling the whole tree is available. Dedicated cached sibling values and ancestor-only updater are absent.

mechanisms.summary: Shape classes, acyclic unlimited schedules and amortization thresholds
boundaries: Backend batching availability and measured per-use/setup costs are supplied. Unlimited-resource critical path is not a finite-device optimal scheduling theorem.

mechanisms.summary: Matched case/output/reference/timing contracts and retained negative outcomes
boundaries: Historical paper CPU/GPU corpus is source evidence, not rerun here. No fresh GPU throughput claim; timing conclusions require matched scopes and environments.

mechanisms.summary: NumPy/CuPy packet execution and backend qualification
boundaries: CuPy is optional. CPU test success does not establish a GPU is present or qualify a hardware performance claim.

mechanisms.summary: Unrestricted structure discovery, nonadditive compilation and packet-native architecture
boundaries: The paper does not prove universal approximation guarantees or universal communication improvements for these broader problems.
